text: People. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether customers or otherwise. <break time="0.8s" /> Want to feel heard. <break time="0.8s" /> When someone calls customer service. <break time="0.8s" /> Asks to speak to a manager. <break time="0.8s" /> Or comes into your office. <break time="0.8s" /> With something on their mind. <break time="0.8s" /> They want to feel like. <break time="0.8s" /> Someone is listening to their concerns. <break time="0.8s" /> And going to address them. <break time="0.8s" /> But for someone to feel heard. <break time="0.8s" /> Three things have to happen. <break time="0.8s" /> First. <break time="0.8s" /> They have to feel like. <break time="0.8s" /> The other person paid attention. <break time="0.8s" /> To what they said. <break time="0.8s" /> Second. <break time="0.8s" /> They have to feel like. <break time="0.8s" /> The other person understood what they said. <break time="0.8s" /> And third. <break time="0.8s" /> The other person has to demonstrate. <break time="0.8s" /> That they listened. <break time="0.8s" /> This last part is key. <break time="0.8s" /> Imagine talking to someone. <break time="0.8s" /> Who provided no response. <break time="0.8s" /> They might have attended. <break time="0.8s" /> To everything we said. <break time="0.8s" /> They might even have understood it completely. <break time="0.8s" /> But without some sort of outward signal that indicates they listened. <break time="0.8s" /> It is impossible to know. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether or not they actually did.
